newsitem.title: CANADA: Window seen open for higher Wascana bid.
newsitem.headline: Window seen open for higher Wascana bid.

text.p: Wascana Energy Inc could coax a rival bidder to step forward now that it has rejected Talisman Energy Inc's C$1.7 billion takeover offer and has released rosier financials, analysts said on Wednesday.
Regina, Saskatchewan-based Wascana, fighting to prove its turnaround is even better than expected, may also be buoyed by a recent drop in Talisman's share price.

"Now that Talisman shares have come off and Wascana has said it's got all this potential, if somebody buys into that potential...this opens opens the window for another bidder," Matt Janisch, analyst with Nesbitt Burns, said.
Wascana chief executive Frank Proto on Tuesday produced production and financial estimates for 1998 that were well beyond most analyst forecasts.

The numbers, which are likely be moot because Wascana is in play, were updated after the company's oil and gas reserves were revised upward from previously released 1996 results in an evaluation conducted by Ryder Scott Co.
Proven plus probable reserves were deemed 24 percent higher than previously reported.
Especially large reserve and production gains were expected to come from Wascana's Smiley-Buffalo heavy oil discovery in west-central Saskatchewan.
Proto said the company's potential for growth was a main reason behind the bid rejection.
However, some analysts said they had difficulty ramping up their own cash flow targets for 1998 to Wascana's expected C$4.89 per share based on the new data.

"It will be interesting to see where after-tax values come out on this thing, and clearly Wascana has some explanations to make as to how they can possibly get to C$4.89 a share in cash flow, because I can't get there," Martin Molyneaux, analyst with FirstEnergy Capital Corp said.
Talisman has offered C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share. However, a recent slide in Talisman's share price has dropped the exchange value below the cash amount.
Wascana stock, meanwhile, climbed to above C$19 a share after its management served notice it would put up a strong fight and the market appeared to bet on a higher bid surfacing.
Janisch said the Talisman bid looked much richer when its net value was above C$18.70, as apposed to the current level of about C$18.25.

A cash bid of between C$18.75 and C$19 could win the day, he said. Other analysts speculated that potential higher offers could be above C$20. However, Talisman's share value, seen as good as or better than cash because of its growth potential and liquidity, was seen to be the wild card.
"It could be touch and go. If Talisman shares go on a little run, they'll be at (C$18.75) or higher, he said. "Whereas if it's a competing paper offer it would have to beat it more substancially."

Several companies have recently been speculated as potential white knights for Wascana, including Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, Husky Oil Ltd and most recently Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd.
Still unknown is how Wascana's will board will rule on Talisman's requests to meet with Wascana's board and gain access to it data rooms, and how such a move may affect the bid price.
Wascana shares on Wednesday closed up 0.05 to 19.15. Talisman gained 0.30 to close at 44.50.
